title: Missing the Margins: A Systematic Literature Review on the Demographic Representativeness of LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Systematic literature review analyzing how empirical studies evaluate gender representativeness, including the operationalization of binary and diverse/marginalized gender categories.
Systematic literature review of papers assessing LLM representativeness of racial and ethnic groups, examining the inclusion of subcategories and diverse demographic descriptors.
Systematic literature review categorizing how previous studies operationalize and evaluate age demographics and generational subgroups in LLMs.
Systematic literature review tracking how educational attainment levels are studied and evaluated for demographic representativeness in LLMs.
Systematic literature review examining the evaluation and representation of various religious identities and affiliations in LLM applications.
Systematic literature review of studies evaluating political leaning and ideological representativeness in LLMs using prompt-induced personas.
Systematic literature review analyzing how class, income, and overall socioeconomic status are operationalized and evaluated in LLM research.
Systematic literature review tracking the evaluation and simulation of immigrant, migrant worker, and undocumented status representations in LLMs.
Systematic literature review of location-based demographic evaluations, tracking the geographical regions and continents represented by LLM personas.
Systematic literature review examining the target populations and specific nationalities evaluated in LLMs, specifically tracking the outsized focus on U.S. populations versus global representation.
Systematic literature review tracking the inclusion and evaluation of sexuality and LGBTQ+ subgroups in studies assessing LLM representativeness.
Systematic literature review of papers assessing the representativeness and potential stereotyping of physical and mental disability statuses in LLMs.
